reasoning: Both sets are strong on quant method. Each fits factors and denoising per window, records hypotheses before running them, corrects for multiple tests and runs the null-hypothesis-testing skill on every feature and portfolio claim. Each also turns the full-sample PCA in market_decomposition.py into a per-window fit. A covers every stage the user asked for. Its Stage 4 has PPO agents with a configuration budget registered in advance, a rented GPU with a spending cap and verified teardown, a held-back lockbox and a final verdict. Its one M1 plan is compact and readable, with 27 synthetic known-answer golden cases for the data stage and a sound dependency graph. A's main gaps: it leaves out the yahooquery cross-check and the user's list of 10 delisted names, and it has no CONSTRAINTS.md even though every packet points to it. B handles Stage 1 better: it has the Yahoo cross-check, a check against the 10-name list, CONSTRAINTS.md and idea files. But B removes PPO agents from Stage 4 and forbids cloud compute, claiming 'as the brief requires', which contradicts the user's rented GPU. Its brief is still worded for Stage 1 only. Its plan labels many 'spine' tasks as Kind thicken / Mode split ('fold'), and it has no golden cases for qdata. It is also much longer (a 744-line spec, 10 milestones). Weighing these, A's tighter and more complete research arc edges out B's better data-stage fidelity.
